summary:
This joint resolution invokes the expedited congressional disapproval procedure under the Congressional Review Act (CRA), codified at chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code (5 U.S.C. §§ 801 et seq.), to nullify a rule promulgated by the Department of Education.

The operative mechanism is a resolution of disapproval under 5 U.S.C. § 802. The single operative clause provides that Congress disapproves the identified agency action and that "such rule shall have no force or effect." Upon enactment (presentment to and signature by the President, or override of a veto), the effect under 5 U.S.C. § 801(b)(1) is that the rule is treated as though it had never taken effect; under § 801(b)(2), a rule so disapproved may not be reissued in substantially the same form, nor a new rule that is substantially the same be issued, absent subsequent authorizing legislation.

The targeted action is the Department of Education measure relating to "Waivers and Modifications of Federal Student Loans." The resolution identifies the action comprehensively, encompassing (1) the website announcement titled "One-Time Federal Student Loan Debt Relief"; and (2) the Federal Register document titled "Federal Student Aid Programs (Federal Perkins Loan Program, Federal Family Education Loan Program, and William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan Program)," 87 Fed. Reg. 61512 (Oct. 12, 2022).

The resolution recites procedural predicates supporting its treatment of the measure as a "rule" subject to CRA review. It references the rule as printed in the Congressional Record on March 22, 2023, at pages S903–S906, together with a Government Accountability Office letter of opinion dated March 17, 2023, concluding that the Waivers and Modifications constitute a "rule" under the CRA. This GAO opinion is material because it addresses the threshold jurisdictional question of whether the agency action qualifies as a rule triggering the CRA's submission requirements and disapproval mechanism—particularly given that the underlying measure was not formally submitted to Congress as a rule.

The resolution contains no amendments to the United States Code, no authorizations or appropriations, no sunset provisions, and no severability clause. It effects no substantive amendment to any statute; its sole legal consequence is the invalidation of the specified agency action pursuant to the CRA.

The measure passed the House of Representatives on May 24, 2023, and was received in the Senate on May 30, 2023. As a joint resolution, it requires passage by both chambers and presentment to the President to take effect.
